enplanements.methodology: 5-year CAGR = (CY2024 / CY2019)^(1/5) - 1, per ticket #3's COVID-safe methodology (skips the 2020-2022 pandemic collapse/recovery years by construction).

capacity.methodology: runway-count-based heuristic: annualPassengerCapacity = openRunwayCount * 10,000,000. The 10M/runway constant is derived from: FAA AC 150/5060-5 'Airport Capacity and Delay' benchmark hourly capacity of ~50-60 operations/hour for a single independently-operated runway; assumed practical annual utilization of ~250,000 operations/year for a well-utilized single runway (consistent with the range single-runway airports such as London Gatwick, the world's busiest single-runway airport, approach in practice); and a blended US industry average of ~85 enplaned passengers per departure (roughly half of all operations) from BTS/FAA air carrier statistics. 250,000 ops * 0.5 * 85 pax ~= 10.6M, rounded to 10M for a clean uniform constant applied identically to every airport regardless of runway configuration, aircraft mix, or terminal/gate constraints. This is an explicit planning-level estimate, not an authoritative figure -- actual terminal design capacity is not published in any public dataset (see ticket #3 resolution).
capacity.source: Derived heuristic; see methodology field. Anchor benchmarks: FAA AC 150/5060-5; industry commentary on Gatwick's single-runway throughput (~40-45M annual passengers, ~275-285k annual movements) as an upper-bound reference point.

routeMix.definition: Share of unique nonstop scheduled passenger destinations at >=2000 statute miles great-circle distance from the airport (a destination-count proxy for BTS T-100 passenger-weighted long-haul mix; see confidence note).
routeMix.methodology: BTS T-100 Domestic/International Segment microdata (which would give a true flight/passenger-weighted long-haul share) is not fetchable by an automated script in this environment: the TranStats web UI requires an interactive multi-step form submission with no documented direct-download URL, and the Socrata-based datahub.transportation.gov API for the same table returns 'You must be logged in to access this resource' for unauthenticated requests. As a pragmatic 1-day-scope substitute, long-haul share is approximated from each airport's current unique nonstop destination list (~62 destinations for ANC as of Aug 2026, per FlightConnections/Flightradar24), counting destinations with typical nonstop distance >=2000 miles. For ANC this is essentially one route: Condor's Anchorage-Frankfurt service (~4,330 mi), plus occasional seasonal Alaska Airlines Honolulu service. Despite ANC being one of the world's busiest CARGO airports by landed weight, its PASSENGER long-haul share is low -- most passenger traffic is short/medium-haul intra-Alaska and Lower-48 connections.
routeMix.source: FlightConnections/Flightradar24 destination lists (accessed Aug 2026); distance classification by author

delay.metric: approx. % of scheduled flights arriving >15 minutes late
delay.methodology: BTS On-Time Performance / Air Travel Consumer Report per-airport annual rankings could not be bulk-downloaded in this environment (bts.gov and transportation.gov PDF/XLSX report links return HTTP 403 to automated fetches; the Socrata datahub.transportation.gov API requires login). National CY2024 baseline was independently confirmed via press synthesis of BTS data: 20.3% of scheduled domestic flights delayed >15min, 78.10% on-time arrival rate. ANC's estimate is set below the national baseline because it is a medium-hub airport without ANC-specific commercial passenger operations at the intensity that drives delay at major connecting hubs (its congestion, when it occurs, is more often cargo-ramp/weather driven and not well captured by passenger OTP frameworks).
delay.source: BTS Air Travel Consumer Report / national CY2024 on-time performance baseline (20.3% delayed, 78.1% on-time), via https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/air-travel-consumer-report-december-2024-full-year-2024-numbers and press synthesis; airport-specific figure is an estimate, not a directly reported BTS number.

notes: Verified as having meaningful, year-round certificated-carrier commercial passenger service (FAA CY2024 enplanements: 2,767,856; FAA hub classification: Medium hub) -- retained in the full tier as one of the assignment's 4 mandatory test-case airports.

Capacity-utilization ratio likely UNDERSTATES ANC's true operational congestion: a large share of ANC's runway capacity is consumed by all-cargo widebody freighter operations (ANC is consistently ranked among the world's top 5 cargo airports by landed weight), which this passenger-only heuristic does not account for.

enplanements.methodology: 5-year CAGR = (CY2024 / CY2019)^(1/5) - 1, per ticket #3's COVID-safe methodology (skips the 2020-2022 pandemic collapse/recovery years by construction).
enplanements.source: FAA CY2019 and CY2024 Passenger Boarding (Enplanement) Data for U.S. Airports, fetched live at build time from faa.gov

capacity.methodology: runway-count-based heuristic: annualPassengerCapacity = openRunwayCount * 10,000,000. Same uniform constant and derivation as the full tier -- see data/full-tier.json's ANC record for the full FAA AC 150/5060-5-based derivation chain.
capacity.source: Derived heuristic (see methodology field); not a published per-airport figure.

routeMix.definition: Share of unique nonstop scheduled passenger destinations at >=2000 statute miles great-circle distance from the airport (a destination-count proxy for BTS T-100 passenger-weighted long-haul mix).
routeMix.methodology: Pragmatic 1-day-scope simplification, lower confidence than the full tier's already-estimated figures: BTS T-100 segment microdata is not fetchable by this script (TranStats requires an interactive form submission with no documented direct-download URL; see module doc comment). Value is a hardcoded estimate from published route maps. Mostly domestic with a small and recently-growing transatlantic network.
routeMix.source: Hardcoded lookup table in scripts/build-screening-tier.ts (LONG_HAUL_AND_DELAY_ESTIMATES), built from published route maps (FlightConnections/Wikipedia, accessed Aug 2026).

delay.methodology: Pragmatic 1-day-scope simplification, lower confidence than the full tier's already-estimated figures: BTS On-Time Performance microdata requires an authenticated Socrata API call (datahub.transportation.gov returns "You must be logged in") and the bts.gov/transportation.gov summary report downloads return HTTP 403 to automated fetches; see module doc comment. Value is anchored to the real CY2024 national baseline (20.3% of flights delayed) and adjusted per airport. Mostly domestic with a small and recently-growing transatlantic network.
delay.source: Hardcoded lookup table in scripts/build-screening-tier.ts (LONG_HAUL_AND_DELAY_ESTIMATES); national baseline from BTS Air Travel Consumer Report CY2024.

notes: Screening tier: pulled programmatically by scripts/build-screening-tier.ts, not hand-curated. Runway/coordinate data and enplanements/CAGR are freshly fetched from OurAirports and FAA at build time (confidence: sourced); long-haul share and delay rate are a lower-confidence hardcoded estimate (confidence: estimated) -- see the methodology fields above.
